item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.14 (build 874) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.14 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.14-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new: Classroom (File › Classroom)

  • Teachers: create a class and share its join code or QR code (Show on Projector puts it on the big screen). Post the circuit you have open as an assignment, with an optional answer key, and choose whether students can check their own work. See who handed in what, with each one's check result, and download them all.
  • Live class: Go Live puts your circuit on every student's screen. Ask a prediction ("what will the lights show?"), watch the answers come in, then Reveal.
  • Students: join with the code and your name, open an assignment as your own copy, check it if your teacher allows, and hand it in. When your teacher is live, a banner lets you follow along. Students can also join from the website, on an iPad, Chromebook or phone.
  • No accounts: everything is encrypted so only the teacher can read names and hand-ins.
  • From 0.3.13: presenter mode shows your pointer and selection, pulse-button clocks, drawing width control.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.13 (build 871) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.13 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.13-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • Presenter mode shows what you're doing. Your audience now sees your mouse pointer (with a ring when you click), what you select, the drag-select box, the part or wire you're moving, and wires being connected. If you're building in the normal editing view, they see the editing view. They only see Simulation View when you're in Simulation View.
  • A pulse button as the clock. In New from Template, flip-flops and registers can use a Single-Pulse Generator button as their Clock: click it to clock the circuit once.
  • Drawing width is easier to find. The drawing bar has a Width control, and 1, 2 and 3 pick thin, medium and thick. A plain trackpad has no pressure, so lines are a steady medium width.
  • Never stuck after opening a circuit. Questions from Your Circuits can no longer get stuck behind a hidden window, a newly opened circuit takes the keyboard at once, and View › Make This Window Editable clears Lock, Draw, Simulation View and any stuck state.
  • From 0.3.12: drawing, notes, Step Clock (K), Predict and Projector mode, Lock in Place, Check My Circuit for clocked circuits, timing worksheets and new templates.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.12 (build 866) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.12 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.12-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new (for teaching)

  • Draw on the circuit. Press the pencil in the toolbar (or ⌥⌘P) and draw right on your circuit with a pen, highlighter or eraser. Drawings stay pinned to the circuit, are saved with it, and can be shown or hidden (⇧⌘H). Mouse, trackpad and Wacom pens all work; a Wacom pen's pressure changes the line width.
  • Presenter mode (⇧⌘P). With a projector or second screen plugged in, View › Present On puts a clean full-screen view of your circuit on it, following your editor live, so you can keep working on your laptop. With one screen, Present in This Window goes full-screen.
  • Notes (⌥⌘N). A notes pane for each circuit, saved with it. They can go in your lab report.
  • Step Clock (K). A clock can be set to move only when you step it, one full cycle at a time. The flip-flop templates use it.
  • Predict, then reveal and Projector mode in Simulation View, for lectures.
  • Lock in Place. Lock the starter parts so students can only wire between them.
  • Check My Circuit for clocked circuits: counters and state machines, with the first wrong clock step shown.
  • Timing diagram worksheets: leave signals blank for students to fill in.
  • New templates: every flip-flop and latch, five registers, and four "what's wrong here?" circuits.
  • Drawing and notes are saved in the circuit file. Older versions of CedarLogic open those files, but drop the drawing and notes if they save.

Please try

Presenter mode on a second screen, drawing with a Wacom pen or trackpad, and everything above.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.11 (build 820) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.11 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.11-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • A template for every flip-flop and latch. File › New from Template has a new Flip-Flops and Latches section: D, D falling edge, D with clock enable, J-K, J-K falling edge, T, an SR latch and a gated D latch. Each one is ready to run, with a clock, a switch on every input and lights on Q and Q'. The PRE' and CLR' switches start on because they're active low: turn one off to set or clear Q at once.
  • From 0.3.10: quitting works again with sync on.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.10 (build 818) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.10 (beta)

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.10-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • Quitting works again with sync on. After the "Quit CedarLogic?" question, the app could get stuck and never close. It now sends your last changes and quits.
  • From 0.3.9: after the synced copy is reset, every device shows up in Settings › Sync › Devices again right away, and the "synced circuits are damaged" note clears.
  • From 0.3.8: link this Mac by scanning, no typing. Settings › Sync › I Have a Code shows a QR code: scan it with CedarLogic on a phone that syncs (Your Circuits › Sync › Add a Device), then press Link here.

item.description:
CedarLogic for Mac 0.3.9 (beta)

CedarLogic-0.3.9-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • Sync fixes. After the synced copy is reset (Start Over, or a reset on the website), every device shows up in Settings › Sync › Devices again right away, instead of a day later or not at all. And the "synced circuits are damaged" note now goes away once those circuits are gone from the synced copy.
  • From 0.3.8: link this Mac by scanning, no typing. Settings › Sync › I Have a Code shows a QR code. On a phone that syncs, open CedarLogic › Your Circuits › Sync › Add a Device and scan it, then press Link here.

item.description:

Download

CedarLogic-0.3.8-Mac.dmg below: open it and drag CedarLogic into Applications. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon. The first time you open it, macOS may ask you to confirm: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

What's new

  • Link this Mac to your sync by scanning, no typing. Settings › Sync › I Have a Code now shows a QR code. On a phone that syncs, open CedarLogic › Your Circuits › Sync › Add a Device and scan it: the phone sends this Mac your sync code (end-to-end encrypted), and you press Link. Typing or pasting the code still works too.

item.title: CedarLogic 0.3.7 (build 802) beta
item.description:
CedarLogic 0.3.7

  • Sync Your Circuits across your devices. Settings › Sync › Turn On Sync gives you a sync code (and a QR code). Enter it on your other Mac, your Raspberry Pi, your Windows PC or CedarLogic Online on your phone, and your circuits follow you. They're end-to-end encrypted: the website stores them but can't read them.
  • When two devices change the same circuit, nothing is lost: the newer one becomes the circuit and the other is kept in Version History.
